text:
maria: Quick heads-up — I brought up `heron-v2-emb` (int8, per-channel) on staging and ran a quick onboarding sweep against wiki-short-span. Seeing a noticeable drop on short queries (~7% R@10 delta vs fp16). Sharing the minimal numbers I ran locally.

maria: ```
metric         | baseline(fp16) | int8-perchannel
recall@1       | 0.72           | 0.68
recall@5       | 0.89           | 0.84
recall@10      | 0.93           | 0.86
mean_cosine    | 0.412          | 0.379
```

alex: Can you paste the eval command and the subset you ran? Also, any preprocessing differences vs baseline (norm/whiten/truncation)?

maria: Ran with our standard `embed_eval` harness: `embed_eval --model heron-v2-emb --repr int8 --dataset wiki-short --k 1,5,10 --save-failures /tmp/failures.json`
No preprocessing changes — normalization enabled in the eval pipeline. Sequence length 512.

sam: Two quick suspects: 1) quant calibration set mismatch (short queries distribution) and 2) subtle whitening shift after quant. Can you dump failure pairs (query + nearest doc) for a few examples?

maria: Pasted 3 representative failures from failures.json below:

maria: 1) query: "what causes tides"
expected top doc: "tidal forces and moon"
actual top doc: "ocean layers and salinity"

maria: 2) query: "symptoms of iron deficiency"
expected top doc: "anemia symptoms"
actual top doc: "dietary iron sources"

leila: Are these short ambiguous queries or multi-sentence? If embedding norm scale changed slightly, short queries get hit harder. Try comparing L2 norms distribution between fp16 and int8 for queries under 8 tokens.

alex: Also run the same eval but with `--normalize false` to check whether normalization is masking a magnitude shift. If normalization hides differences, we may have numeric instability in KV cache or pre-layers after quant.

ci-bot: [auto-test] nightly-embed-regressions ran at 2026-03-20T04:12:03Z — no regressions flagged for long queries, short-query suite flagged 1 failure set (same model). Link: https://ci.redwood/embedded/4467890123

sam: If it's calibration, try a micro-run with a calibration set sampled from short queries (e.g., 10k short). Also compare per-channel vs per-tensor and symmetric vs asymmetric quantization. Sometimes per-tensor can be more stable for very short sequences.

maria: Good point — current build used per-channel int8 symmetric. I'll spin quick variants: per-tensor symmetric, per-channel asymmetric. Will run 10k short holdout.

leila: After you have runs, generate a small diag: distribution of top-1 cosines, L2 norms, and pairwise cosine delta between fp16 and int8 for same query. A one-pager plot helps. Also run UMAP of embeddings for a subset to eyeball cluster drift.

alex: If those checks still look bad, run PCA on token representations before pool and compare explained variance. Sometimes quantization collapses variance in earlier dims and that affects short-query semantics.

maria: Copying commands I'll use: 
```
# baseline
embed_eval --model heron-v2-emb --repr fp16 --dataset wiki-short --k 1,5,10 --out baseline.json
# int8 variants
embed_eval --model heron-v2-emb --repr int8-perchannel --dataset wiki-short --k 1,5,10 --out int8_pc.json
embed_eval --model heron-v2-emb --repr int8-pertensor --dataset wiki-short --k 1,5,10 --out int8_pt.json
# diagnostics
python tools/diag_embed_diff.py --base baseline.json --variant int8_pc.json --out diag_pc.pdf --sample-size 5000
```

maria: I'll upload results to the ci link and ping back here. tagging @leila @sam for cluster and calibration checks :eyes: :rocket:

sam: Thanks — if you can include the calibration code (seed + subset) we can try grid search over clip thresholds quickly. Also might be worth testing int6 in a pinch; earlier model X tolerated int6 with minimal perf loss.

leila: Also check tokenizer edge cases — if short queries have punctuation the tokenizer might produce different token splits vs our baseline run (rare but seen before).

alex: Great triage plan. If we confirm it's mainly magnitude shift, a small retrain or adding a post-quant gain/scale correction layer usually recovers most of the gap. Keep notes on wall-clock perf too (throughput/latency).

maria: Will do. I'll post results snapshot in ~2 hours.
